title: Decoding the elite soccer player’s psychological profile
affected_claim: Elite soccer players exhibit reduced agreeableness, a feature interpreted as potentially advantageous in intense competition.
evidence_summary: Author response identifies incorrect reverse scoring affecting four of six Agreeableness items (and one Openness item), not merely unusual correlations. The original abstract and discussion prominently characterize elite players as less agreeable. Authors acknowledge that the scoring correction substantially changes Agreeableness scores and that their revised personality analysis yields the opposite direction. This materially undermines that original substantive personality claim independently of unresolved broad data-integrity allegations. Only a small subset of questionnaires was recovered. Authors fit calibration models to that subset and apply them elsewhere, then compare players against German norms instead of original Brazilian controls. Therefore neither the exact corrected effect nor reversal of the original matched-control contrast is independently established. The narrow qualifying error is wrong scoring invalidating an emphasized original trait interpretation; fabrication and global dataset invalidity remain unproven.
